evals.prompt: We're almost out of context. Over this session we wrote docs/specs/export-v2.md, a plan at docs/plans/export-v2.md (tasks 1-4 done, 5-8 left), decided to use streaming CSV instead of building the file in memory because of the 2GB customer, and found that the S3 client retries break idempotency. The .env has AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=AKIA... that I pasted earlier. Write a handoff so tomorrow's session can continue.
evals.expected_output: A handoff document that gathers the git state and references the spec and plan by path without copying them. It records the streaming decision and the S3 retry finding, redacts the AWS secret, lists concrete next steps starting at plan task 5, suggests skills, and saves the document outside the repo.
expectations: Runs git commands (status/log/diff) to capture actual state rather than writing it from memory
References docs/specs/export-v2.md and docs/plans/export-v2.md by path instead of reproducing their contents
Records the streaming-CSV decision with its reason and the S3 retry/idempotency finding
Does not include the AWS secret value; uses a placeholder or env var name
Next steps start at plan task 5 with a concrete file or command
Saves the file outside the working tree (e.g. OS temp dir) and tells the user the path

evals.prompt: Hand this off to my teammate who'll pick up the flaky checkout test tomorrow. They won't have this chat.
evals.expected_output: A handoff tailored to the flaky checkout test: the current repro rate or command, the hypotheses already ruled out, and where to start. It is written for someone with no chat history.
expectations: Puts the flaky checkout test focus first and omits unrelated session detail
States the reproduction command and the last observed result
Lists approaches already tried and why they failed
The first next step is actionable without asking a question

evals.prompt: Here's the handoff from yesterday's session (in /tmp/handoff-billing.md). Pick it up and keep going.
evals.expected_output: The receiving agent verifies the recorded state (branch, SHA, last check) before acting. It reads only the listed files, respects recorded decisions, and starts at the first next step.
expectations: Compares current git state against the handoff's State section
Re-runs the recorded last check before building on it
Does not re-litigate recorded decisions or retry recorded failed approaches without new evidence
Starts work at the handoff's first next step
